issues.legal_issue: A party affected by an order cannot treat it as non-binding merely because the party considers it void or invalid.
material_facts: The appellants challenged the validity of a notification affecting their land, arguing that it did not state the source of authority and that the required legal procedure had not been followed.
The validity of the notification was pending consideration in a civil suit, and the Court declined to decide that challenge in these proceedings.
issues.conclusion: Even an order or notification alleged to be void or voidable remains binding unless and until a competent court sets it aside or declares it invalid; a party cannot decide for itself to disregard it.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on State of Kerala v. M.K. Kunhikannan Nambiar, AIR 1996 SC 906; Tayabbhai M. Bagasarwalla v. Hind Rubber Industries Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1997 SC 1240; M. Meenakshi v. Metadin Agarwal, (2006) 7 SCC 470; Sneh Gupta v. Devi Sarup, (2009) 6 SCC 194; State of Punjab v. Gurdev Singh, AIR 1991 SC 2219; and Sultan Sadik v. Sanjay Raj Subba, AIR 2004 SC 1377. It also referred to Lord Radcliffe’s observation in Smith v. East Elloe Rural District Council, [1956] 1 All ER 855, that an order remains effective for its ostensible purpose unless proceedings establish its invalidity and obtain its setting aside or other relief.

predicates.party_affected_by_order: A person or entity is affected by an order made by an authority or court.
predicates.order_validity_disputed: The affected person or entity disputes the order’s validity or binding effect.

issues.definition: When an affected party disputes an order’s validity, it must obtain a court declaration before disregarding the order.

issues.legal_issue: Salt harvesting by solar evaporation is not permitted in an ecologically sensitive area that contains mangroves.
material_facts: The disputed land contained mangrove forest and was ecologically sensitive.

The applicable coastal regulations classified mangroves as an ecologically sensitive category and allowed salt harvesting by solar evaporation in that category only where the area was not ecologically sensitive and important.
The land had not been used for salt manufacturing for more than two decades.
issues.conclusion: Salt harvesting by solar evaporation could not be permitted on the disputed land because it was an ecologically sensitive area containing mangroves.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the Coastal Regulation Zone Regulations, 1991. Those regulations place mangroves within CRZ-I and permit salt harvesting by solar evaporation there only in areas that are not ecologically sensitive and important.

predicates.coastal_zone_regulatory_case: The proceeding concerns the regulation of activity in a coastal zone.
predicates.area_is_ecologically_sensitive_mangrove_: The area contains mangroves and is ecologically sensitive.
predicates.salt_harvesting_proposed: A party proposes to harvest salt by solar evaporation in the area.

issues.definition: In a coastal-zone case, a proposal to harvest salt is not permitted when the area is an ecologically sensitive mangrove habitat.

issues.legal_issue: Deliberate conduct that exceeds permission to repair a structure and damages mangroves or obstructs natural water flow constitutes willful disobedience of the applicable orders.
material_facts: The appellants were permitted to repair an existing bund, subject to conditions that they carry out no other construction, not destroy mangroves or vegetation, and not raise the bund’s existing height.

Inspection reports and a court-directed site inspection found that the appellants had widened and raised the bund, built platforms, dumped debris and boulders, closed culverts, obstructed the natural flow of water, and cut or damaged mangroves.
The reports described the work as extensive and the Court found the disobedience deliberate.
issues.conclusion: The appellants were guilty of willful defiance of the Court’s orders and the District Collector’s order, and the contempt proceedings brought against them were allowed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated contempt proceedings as quasi-criminal and found that the documented, deliberate departures from the repair-only permission and its conditions established contumacious conduct. It also held that an unlawful action cannot be validated by describing it as repair work.

rule.if: contempt_proceeding_for_order_disobedience and permission_limited_to_repair_existing_structure and conditions_prohibited_expansion_or_ecological_damage and (party_expanded_structure_or_blocked_water_flow or party_damaged_protected_vegetation) and inspection_evidence_confirmed_violations

predicates.contempt_proceeding_for_order_disobedien: The proceeding alleges disobedience of an order made by a court or public authority.
predicates.permission_limited_to_repair_existing_st: A party was allowed to repair an existing structure, rather than to undertake new or expanded construction.
predicates.conditions_prohibited_expansion_or_ecolo: The permission required the party not to expand the structure or damage protected vegetation or ecological conditions.
predicates.party_expanded_structure_or_blocked_wate: The party expanded the structure or obstructed the natural flow of water while carrying out the work.
predicates.party_damaged_protected_vegetation: The party cut, destroyed, or otherwise damaged protected vegetation while carrying out the work.
predicates.inspection_evidence_confirmed_violations: Inspection evidence confirmed the prohibited work or resulting ecological damage.

issues.definition: A party is guilty of willful contempt when inspection evidence confirms that, despite repair-only permission and conditions against expansion or ecological damage, the party deliberately expands the structure, blocks natural water flow, or damages protected vegetation.

issues.legal_issue: After finding deliberate disobedience that altered a structure and harmed natural water flow or vegetation, the Court may direct restoration and require the responsible party to bear the cost of enforcement if it fails to comply.
material_facts: The bund had been raised and widened, debris and boulders had been used in its construction, and platforms had been built.
Culverts and drains that had facilitated the natural flow of sea water had been closed, and mangroves had been damaged or had died.

The Court directed the appellants to restore the bund’s former height and width, remove debris and other materials, dismantle the platforms, and restore the culverts and drains; it authorized the District Collector to carry out the work and recover its cost if the appellants failed to do so.
issues.conclusion: The appellants were directed to restore the bund and the former water channels; if they failed to do so within the stipulated time, the District Collector was to carry out the restoration and recover the cost from them.
issues.legal_principle: As relief for the established contempt and environmental harm, the Court ordered removal of the additions and materials, restoration of the earlier bund dimensions and water channels, and enforcement at the responsible party’s cost in the event of non-compliance.

predicates.contempt_proceeding_for_order_disobedien: The proceeding alleges disobedience of an order made by a court or public authority.
predicates.deliberate_alteration_caused_ecological_: A party deliberately altered a structure and the alteration damaged vegetation or obstructed natural water flow.
predicates.restoration_of_prior_condition_is_feasib: The previous structure and natural water channels can be restored by removing or reversing the alterations.

issues.definition: When deliberate alterations causing ecological harm can be reversed, the responsible party must restore the prior condition.

issues.legal_issue: A public official does not commit contempt merely by investigating and directing corrective action to enforce conditions imposed on a party.
material_facts: The District Collector had permitted repair subject to conditions protecting the existing bund and mangroves.

After receiving complaints and inspection findings of violations, the Collector appointed a committee to investigate and directed corrective measures, including removing material used to raise the bund and restoring water flow.
The appellants alleged that the Collector’s actions violated the Court’s orders.
issues.conclusion: The appellants’ contempt petition against the District Collector was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court found the appellants’ allegations against the authorities unwarranted on the facts and treated the authorities’ actions as responses to reported violations of the conditions governing the repair permission.

predicates.contempt_proceeding_against_public_offic: The proceeding alleges that a public official disobeyed a court order.
predicates.official_investigated_reported_noncompli: The official investigated reported breaches of conditions governing permitted work.
predicates.official_directed_measures_to_enforce_ex: The official directed measures intended to enforce those existing conditions.

issues.definition: A contempt petition against an official is dismissed when the official investigates reported non-compliance and directs measures to enforce existing conditions.
